AB 723, also known as the "Deepfake Liability Act of 2019," is a California state bill that was introduced but not enacted. It aimed to address the issue of nonconsensual deepfakes. While the bill did not become law, it provided a useful definition of a "digitally altered image" for the purpose of the proposed legislation.

According to AB 723, a "digitally altered image" is defined as:

"An image, sound recording, animation, or video that (A) is generated through an electronic process that replaces, superimposes, or otherwise modifies the visual or auditory content of an existing image, sound recording, animation, or video, without the consent of all of the individuals who are depicted in the image, sound recording, animation, or video, and (B) is used, intended to be used, or possessed with the intent to be used to harm the reputation or privacy of one or more of those individuals."

This definition emphasizes the manipulation of visual or auditory content without the consent of the individuals depicted and the intent to harm their reputation or privacy. However, it's important to note that AB 723 was not enacted, so this definition is not currently law in California.
